data.name: Home_Tagline
data.value: Your Zwift controllers, your virtual gears, your training app.

data.value: Everything that connects to ShiftBridge: Zwift and other Bluetooth controllers, heart rate sensor, keyboard and gamepads.

data.name: Devices_NoneHint
data.value: Turn the controller off and on again, and disconnect it from Zwift or the phone.

data.name: Devices_NotFoundBody
data.value: Turn it off and on again, and disconnect it from Zwift, the trainer or the phone: a controller only accepts one connection at a time. Locked Click v2 and Ride v2: unlock them via the Zwift app.

data.name: Devices_LocalIntro
data.value: You can also use a keyboard, a remote or a game controller (Xbox, joystick) to shift gears. Assign the buttons in the Buttons tab.

data.name: Devices_SuppressKeys

data.value: Technical log, to attach to your feedback if there is a problem (it also contains the trainer compatibility report).

data.name: Diag_NoteTip
data.value: E.g.: I'm pressing the side button on the left controller

data.name: Apps_Intro
data.value: In your app's controller settings (TrainingPeaks Virtual, Les jeux du cycle), choose “ShiftBridge”.

data.name: Apps_AtLeastOne
data.value: Enable at least one option. Zwift does not use this mode: keep your controllers paired directly with Zwift.

data.name: Apps_TestBody
data.value: Sends a “shift” press to the connected application, to check that it reacts.

data.name: Buttons_AddTip
data.value: Assigns a key from the keyboard, a remote or a game controller

data.name: Buttons_Intro
data.value: Choose the action for each button. The indicator lights up when you press it.

data.name: Buttons_Help
data.value: Keyboard: prefer keys you don't use elsewhere (F13 to F24, media keys, presentation remote). An assigned key is swallowed: it no longer reaches other applications. Game controllers: they cannot be hidden, turn them off in the controlled application to avoid a double trigger.

data.name: Buttons_RepeatTip
data.value: Repeats the gear shift while the button is held down

data.name: Trainer_Intro
data.value: ShiftBridge sits between your trainer and the app to apply virtual gears.

data.name: Trainer_ConnTip
data.value: In your training app: choose “ShiftBridge Trainer” as the trainer (not the trainer directly) and “ShiftBridge” as the controller. Turn off the app's own virtual shifting to avoid doubling up.

data.name: Trainer_BleTip
data.value: Before connecting: close the manufacturer's app on your phone, and do not pair the trainer in your training app or in the Windows Bluetooth settings. A Bluetooth trainer generally accepts only one controller.

data.name: Trainer_GearingTip
data.value: Teeth of the chainring and cog the chain is on (Zwift Cog: 14 teeth, 18 on Elite). Zwift recommends the small chainring. With a big chainring, enter it, otherwise the virtual gears would feel too hard.

data.name: Trainer_ShowOverlay
data.value: Show the virtual gear over the game

data.name: Trainer_OverlayHelp
data.value: Drag to move it, mouse wheel to resize.

data.name: Trainer_Flash
data.value: Flash on each change (red at the limits)

data.name: Trainer_Telemetry
data.value: Trainer power, cadence and speed, plus heart rate

data.name: Trainer_TelemetryTip
data.value: Shown once virtual shifting is active. The speed is the one your app sees (scaled by the virtual gear).

data.name: Trainer_NativeTip
data.value: The trainer applies the gear itself via Zwift's virtual shifting protocol (unofficial, documented by third-party projects). If the trainer doesn't offer it, ShiftBridge automatically falls back to FTMS scaling.

data.name: Trainer_WeightsNote
data.value: Sent to the trainer in native mode. Applied immediately while virtual shifting is active.

data.name: Trainer_GearCountTip
data.value: Fewer gears means bigger steps between them. The range stays the same, from the lightest to the hardest gear. Your current gear moves to the same place on the scale.

data.name: Trainer_ReportGear
data.value: Also send the gear to the app

data.name: Trainer_ReportGearTip
data.value: Experimental (OpenBikeControl “Gear Set”). An app may ignore it, or apply it to its own simulation: if resistance doubles, turn this option off and keep the overlay display.

data.name: Trainer_SlopeOnlyTip
data.value: Turn on if your trainer ignores rolling resistance and drag in the simulation.

data.name: Trainer_AppShiftsTip
data.value: Unchecked (recommended): ShiftBridge applies gears to the trainer and the app never sees them. Checked: ShiftBridge forwards + and − to the app (OpenBikeControl) and relays the trainer without changing anything; the app handles its own virtual gears. Either way, pair your controllers in one place only: a controller also paired in the app (TrainingPeaks Virtual, MyWhoosh…) shifts gears there on its own.

data.name: Onb_WelcomeBody
data.value: ShiftBridge connects your controllers (Zwift Play and Click, Bluetooth remotes, groupsets…) to your training app and adds virtual gears to your smart trainer. This short assistant walks you through three steps: controllers, trainer, app.

data.name: Onb_PermissionsBody
data.value: ShiftBridge uses Bluetooth to talk to your controllers, your trainer and your app. On the next screen, allow “Nearby devices” and notifications: the notification keeps ShiftBridge running during your ride.

data.name: Onb_ControllersBody
data.value: Turn on your controllers (press a button to wake them up): ShiftBridge finds them and connects on its own. You can skip this step and do it later from the Devices page.

data.name: Onb_TrainerBody
data.value: Choose your trainer, over Wi-Fi (DirCon) or Bluetooth: ShiftBridge sits between it and your app to apply the virtual gears. No trainer at hand? Skip this step.

data.name: Onb_AppBody
data.value: In your app (TrainingPeaks Virtual, Les jeux du cycle…), choose “ShiftBridge Trainer” as the trainer and “{0}” as the controller. The indicator below turns green as soon as it connects.

data.name: Onb_DoneBody
data.value: You can change all of this at any time from the Devices, Trainer and App pages. The assistant can be run again from Settings.
